summary.name: Incident Manager On-Call (IMOC) role guide
summary.one_liner: A Gremlin tutorial describing the Incident Manager On-Call (IMOC) role, which leads and coordinates response to high severity incidents (SEVs) through their lifecycle.
keywords: how to define incident manager role
use_cases: Defining an incident manager on-call role within a company
Setting up a 24/7 IMOC rotation for engineering leaders
Training staff to lead SEV 0 incident response
Coordinating company-wide communication during major outages
Tracking incident timelines and responsibilities during SEVs
summary.what_it_does: The page explains the IMOC role, whose main job is to resolve high severity incidents quickly and safely by leading and coordinating the SEV team through detection, diagnosis, mitigation, prevention, and closure. It describes the principles IMOCs follow, such as staying calm, communicating concisely, and maintaining a shared SEV timeline with actions and owners. It outlines how to build a rotation with a primary and secondary IMOC on call for a week at a time, supported by a small IMOC rotation team and monthly syncs. It also lists training topics, such as SEV levels, the lifecycle, past SEV 0 examples, and GameDays, plus recommended tools like a SEV reporting tool, automatic paging with escalation after one minute without acknowledgment, and monitoring dashboards.
notable: Defines IMOC as a single leader per SEV with a primary and secondary on-call rotation
Targets resolving SEV 0 incidents within 15 minutes
Part two of a three-part series on SEV management programs, with a companion post on the Technical Lead On-Call role
caveats: Written as a process guide for establishing the role; it does not describe a software product
Page is promotional for Gremlin at the end; the substantive content is the IMOC process
